messages:
anya (prod): FYI — ACME just escalated. Renewal in 6 weeks. They want 99.95% SLA + ~50ms p50 for hosted text-generation. Sales wants this prioritized immediately.

sam (sales): Confirmed. They're the main renewal at risk, >$1.2M ARR. Legal already asked for SLA clause draft.

maya (cs): ACME says latency issue impacts customer-facing autocomplete. They provided logs showing p50 ~120ms and p95 ~400ms in eu-west.

devon (eng): 50ms p50 for hosted is pretty aggressive for general-purpose models. Need to know: 50ms p50 for which sequence length and model? Token length matters a lot.

liam (platform pm): Good point. We should scope: is ACME demanding 50ms for short prompts (<32 tokens) on our curated small models, or for large context?

anya (prod): From the CS thread: they insisted "production reads/writes" use-case with short prompts (completion + reranking). They called out 32-token median.

zoya (eng mgr): Quick triage: options — 1) carve dedicated low-latency pool (reserved nodes + prewarmed KV cache) for ACME, 2) invest infra work to reduce hosted p50 across customers, 3) propose product workaround (model pinning + quantized variant) while we measure.

devon (eng): Rough RICE calc to compare:
```
Reach = 1 (ACME renewal) -> 1
Impact = 8 (renewal loss ~high) -> 8
Confidence = 0.6 (we can reach 50ms for short prompts?) -> 0.6
Effort = 30 engineering-weeks (infra + perf + testing) -> 30
Score = (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort = (1*8*0.6)/30 ~ 0.16
```
Not great compared to other infra bets that score >0.5.

sam (sales): That math is valid, but renewal revenue and reference value matter more than simple RICE. ACME is a strategic logo for our vertical.

liam (platform pm): Agreed. We should consider a hybrid decision: short-term dedicated pool as a commercial add-on (low engineering time), medium-term roadmap ticket to generalize low-latency offering, long-term invest in kernel/compiler improvements.

zoya (eng mgr): Implementation details for short-term: reserve 4x A10g or H100-backed instances in eu-west, prewarm model instances with pinned model and kv-prefix caching. Add a routing policy to send ACME calls to that pool. Estimated effort: 2 sprints (tech lead + 2 engineers) + ops runbook.

maya (cs): That sounds doable and gives ACME immediate relief. We can attach SLA to the reserved pool and bill as "dedicated latency assurance".

devon (eng): Caveat: capacity overhead and isolation will increase unit cost. Sales/finance must approve pricing that covers it. Also need perf tests that simulate p50 under real traffic.

sam (sales): I'll push a term sheet that includes dedicated pool fees and a 3-month pilot. If they sign, that should buy time for platform work.

anya (prod): Action items: 1) devon/zoya — high-level runbook and perf test plan by EOD tomorrow; 2) liam — add "dedicated low-latency pilot" to next-week roadmap sync and draft rollback criteria; 3) sam/maya — propose pilot commercial terms and timeline to ACME.

zoya (eng mgr): Will do. I'll post a short runbook snippet once we size nodes.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: branch=acme/dedicated-pool, env=staging, requested_by=zoya

sam (sales): :thumbsup: Thanks everyone — I'll try to get verbal sign-off today.

anya (prod): Also note longer-term: we should add SLA-cost playbook to product docs (how to evaluate custom SLAs vs roadmap cost). Will carve an RFC.

liam (platform pm): Agree — add evaluation criteria: revenue, reference value, engineering delta, and strategic fit. We'll codify in prioritization rubric.

maya (cs): One more ask from ACME: data residency in eu-west. Make sure dedicated pool meets that.

zoya (eng mgr): Noted. We'll ensure nodes are in the eu-west tenancy and document data flow.

anya (prod): Last note: keep RICE numbers but also annotate "strategic weight" when a renewal/reference is on the line. We'll discuss in triage tomorrow.

sam (sales): Copy.

(threads ends)
